stories.headline: Yankees' Volpe has grand slam, 5 RBIs in return to majors
stories.summary: Anthony Volpe smacked a grand slam and drove in a career-high five runs during his rousing return from Triple-A as the Yankees beat the Rockies.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- Anthony Volpe's first night back in the majors was one to remember.

Suddenly a fan favorite in New York again, Volpe smacked a grand slam and drove in a career-high five runs during his rousing return from Triple-A as the Yankees beat the Colorado Rockies 10-3 on Thursday.

The much-maligned Volpe is getting another chance with the Yankees -- this time at a new position -- and he's off to a terrific start. With the Bronx crowd chanting his name on several occasions, Volpe had three hits and a stolen base in his first big league game since Aug. 1.

"I wanted to be back up here. I wanted to contribute," Volpe said. "But when you're down there, there's obviously no guarantees. So you work really hard for yourself and for the player that you feel like can help the organization. But other than that, there's nothing guaranteed. You can't control it. So, I never thought I was going to be back here in this moment, but I want to be ready and prepared in case something happens."

Something did happen.

Volpe was recalled from the minors Thursday when second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. went on the 10-day injured list, retroactive to Wednesday, because of a sprained right thumb.

"Unexpected whirlwind, but it feels good to be back," Volpe said.

The 25-year-old Volpe, who lost his shortstop job in New York to 21-year-old rookie George Lombard Jr. last month, made his first big league start at second base and looked rejuvenated.

Batting ninth, he received an enthusiastic ovation from the Yankee Stadium crowd of 40,706 his first time up and laced an RBI single in the second inning before stealing third base. Volpe reached on a hard-hit infield single in the sixth and lined his second big league homer this season over the short porch in right field to make it 10-2 in the seventh.

He finished 3-for-4 and saw 21 pitches at the plate -- 15 during his first two at-bats.

"Good to see the crowd right away behind him," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said.

After rounding the bases in the seventh, Volpe came out of the dugout for a curtain call to salute fans who were chanting his name again.

"Probably a little bit of blackout," Volpe said. "It will be definitely something I'll remember for a long time. ... I didn't really know what was happening."

Slam city

New York didn't have a grand slam all season until Lombard connected in a 6-1 win Wednesday night. It's the first time in franchise history players 25 or younger hit grand slams in consecutive games, according to the Elias Sports Bureau.

The only other regular-season slam for Volpe came in May 2023 against the Athletics. He also had one in the 2024 World Series.

"Excited for him. He hasn't done anything but just continue to work and grind, and got his way back here and obviously had a massive impact tonight," Boone said. "Hopefully something that can springboard him even a little bit more."

Local product

A first-round draft pick in 2019 out of a nearby New Jersey high school, the 5-foot-10 Volpe won a Gold Glove as a rookie shortstop and hit 21 home runs with the Yankees in 2023.

He was expected to hold down the position for years to come, but Volpe entered Thursday with a .224 career batting average, .287 on-base percentage and .660 OPS in four big league seasons. He also has struggled at times on defense, drawing criticism from Yankees fans.

Volpe was optioned to Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre on Aug. 4, with a plan to gain experience at other positions. He played 19 games at second base for the RailRiders and went on a recent tear at the plate.

"He's been excellent, from all the reports from player development," Boone said. "The double-play turn's been excellent. So, not surprised. He's the type of athlete that should take to that position well and so far, so good."

Big numbers in the minors

In his past 28 games at Triple-A, Volpe batted .284 with 10 homers, 21 RBIs, seven doubles, 15 walks and eight steals. He compiled a 1.023 OPS after being demoted.

"It's not an easy thing to go back there and have the right mindset and not only that but go out and perform at a high level, and that's what he did," Boone said. "It's a testament to who he is and his character and I think his love and respect for this game."

Volpe was selected International League Player of the Week for hitting .524 with three homers, six RBIs and five stolen bases over six games from Aug. 31 to Sept. 6. He compiled a 1.674 OPS with five homers over his past eight games for the RailRiders.

"I definitely see a little difference with how he's spread out," Boone said. "I thought he looked really good, really under control, controlled the strike zone, patient at-bats while also obviously delivering some blows."

Then and now

Volpe's season debut for the Yankees was delayed until May 13 after he recovered from surgery last October to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder. He is batting .251 with 24 RBIs in 57 games with New York.

Chisholm can become a free agent after the World Series, so Volpe's chance at second base in a September pennant race could offer something of an audition for next season.

"I just feel like I have an opportunity," Volpe said. "Obviously, it's weird the way it happened. You never want somebody to get hurt or anything, but I had nothing guaranteed, obviously. I thought I was never going to be back up here. So I'm trying to make the most of it."

stories.headline: 49ers rout Rams 27-7 in NFL's first Australia game behind Brock Purdy's 3 TD passes
stories.summary: — The San Francisco 49ers enjoyed every moment of their weeklong Australian adventure. They gradually adjusted their body clocks, enjoyed Melbourne's sights and tastes — and then they dominated a division rival in the NFL's first regular-season game...
stories.body:
MELBOURNE, Australia -- — The San Francisco 49ers enjoyed every moment of their weeklong Australian adventure. They gradually adjusted their body clocks, enjoyed Melbourne's sights and tastes — and then they dominated a division rival in the NFL's first regular-season game Down Under.


The Los Angeles Rams only boomeranged in 28 hours before kickoff, and they flew back out with their Super Bowl aspirations in disarray after getting thrashed in a historic season opener.


Mike Evans, Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel caught touchdown passes from Brock Purdy, and the Niners routed the Rams 27-7 Friday.


Purdy passed for 205 yards against the Rams' ineffective defense at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in front of 100,021 fans, the seventh-largest regular season crowd in NFL history. Australia's sporting capital reveled in its first real taste of American football — and in a dominant win by the 49ers, who had already won many Aussies' affection by traveling to Melbourne a week earlier than the Rams.


“It was definitely worth it to come a little bit early,” said Evans, who caught six passes in a strong 49ers debut. “We definitely got acclimated. ... All the guys attacked it. We didn’t complain. We actually enjoyed being here in Melbourne.”


A party atmosphere prevailed even with a Friday morning kickoff necessary for U.S. television. The fans got another memorable chapter in this NFC West rivalry as the 49ers surprisingly blasted the touted Rams with superior play on both sides of the ball.


San Francisco coach Kyle Shanahan said the historic, hulking arena “felt gladiator-ish. ... It felt like home once we got here. I'm glad the guys played like it, too.”


Kyren Williams scored the NFL’s first Australian touchdown on a 5-yard rush to begin the second quarter, but the 49ers took control from there, scoring the final 24 points.


While Purdy's offense managed enough big plays to win, the San Francisco defense frustrated NFL MVP Matthew Stafford into a 15-of-25 performance for just 155 yards. The Niners defense now led by longtime Rams coordinator Raheem Morris held the NFL's best offense last season to 290 yards and one score, even stopping Stafford on a fourth-down quarterback sneak from the San Francisco 1 in the third quarter.


“Probably only had two good drives, to be honest,” Stafford said. “Not enough good stuff on offense. We didn't do the things that we're accustomed to doing. Too many times, we were on different pages. That starts with me.”


Garrett has a quiet debut
While San Francisco's Fred Warner and Nick Bosa both had big moments in their first games back from lengthy injury absences, Myles Garrett was practically invisible in his Rams debut after missing much of training camp with aches, recording zero tackles. The reigning AP NFL Defensive Player of the Year finally acknowledged after the game that his knee injury has him at less than full health.


“This was the worst version of myself that I’ve put out there, and I’ve got to be better,” Garrett said.


Rams' travel plans are scrutinized
Much of the pregame talk for this trip centered around the teams’ starkly differing methods of preparation: The 49ers ingratiated themselves to the local fans as their body clocks adjusted, while the Rams stayed home until less than two days before kickoff, keeping their body clocks on California time.


“I know there’s gonna be a lot of narratives that appropriately put the blame on me, and then we’ll move forward the right way,” coach Sean McVay said. “I don’t believe (the travel plan) is why we didn’t play well enough. I really don’t.”


Niners take control
Both teams started with understandable sluggishness for a 10:35 a.m. kickoff, but Williams' TD run finally got the crowd cheering. The quarterbacks then traded interceptions before Purdy shook off a shaky start and found former Rams receiver Robinson on a 39-yard post route.


San Francisco surged out of halftime, with Samuel's 45-yard kickoff return leading to Evans' TD catch over new Rams cornerback Jaylen Watson.


The Rams drove deep into the red zone, but after Puka Nacua was ruled down inches outside the goal line, the 49ers stuffed Stafford. San Francisco's responded with a 99-yard drive ending in Samuel's TD grab.


Up next
The 49ers host Miami on Sunday, Sept. 20.


The Rams host the New York Giants on Monday, Sept. 21.

stories.headline: Report: Feds investigating Clippers' Kawhi Leonard dealings
stories.summary: A federal investigation has been opened into the Clippers for allegedly circumventing the NBA's salary cap to compensate Kawhi Leonard, The New York Times reported.
stories.body:
A federal investigation has been opened into the LA Clippers for allegedly circumventing the NBA's salary cap to compensate Kawhi Leonard, The New York Times reported Thursday, citing people briefed on the matter.

The criminal investigation, led by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York in Brooklyn, is in its earliest stages, The Times reported.

A spokesperson for the U.S. Attorney's Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment from ESPN; neither did spokespeople for the Clippers or the NBA.

The investigation follows the NBA's nearly yearlong probe of the Clippers by the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, which "found a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations by the Clippers organization, a prior offender of the salary cap circumvention rules."

The NBA issued a severe punishment for the team, including the loss of five future first-round draft picks, a $30 million fine and a yearlong suspension of owner Steve Ballmer.

At least one subpoena has been issued as part of the investigation by federal prosecutors, The Times reported.

The federal investigation would mark the second instance that a government entity is inquiring about the Clippers and their financial dealings with Leonard, who must pay the NBA $700,000 as part of his punishment.

On Sept. 2, the same day the NBA announced its findings and punishment for the Clippers and Leonard, an executive for scoreboard company Daktronics announced on a quarterly earnings call that it had been contacted by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission about its dealings with Leonard.

The executive said on the call that Daktronics was cooperating and wouldn't comment further.

In the Sept. 2 report from Wachtell Lipton, league investigators said the Clippers directed a kickback from a massive scoreboard contract for Intuit Dome to Leonard in the form of an endorsement deal and even set the terms of a multiyear agreement worth millions of dollars.

The Eastern District of New York has been involved in high-profile NBA investigations for nearly 20 years. In 2007, in collaboration with the FBI, it prosecuted former NBA referee Tim Donaghy, who admitted betting on games he officiated. Donaghy pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to transmit gambling information.

In 2025, the Eastern District indicted then-Portland Trail Blazers coach Chauncey Billups, then-Miami Heat guard Terry Rozier and former NBA guard and assistant coach Damon Jones as part of a pair of wide-ranging investigations related to illegal sports betting and rigged poker games backed by the Mafia.

This year, the office also indicted former NBA players Malik Beasley and Ed Davis as part of an alleged sports betting scheme.

stories.headline: Šeško makes his case for Man United ahead of Manchester derby
stories.summary: Benjamin Šeško's form for Manchester United has given Michael Carrick a selection decision to make ahead of Sunday's Manchester derby.
stories.body:
MANCHESTER, England -- Sabah FK didn't cause Manchester United any problems in their UEFA Champions League opener, but Benjamin Šeško has given Michael Carrick a headache before the Manchester derby.

The Slovenian striker followed up his goal at Everton on Sunday with another against the champions of Azerbaijan at Old Trafford on Thursday. It helped United to a comfortable 4-0 win while also making his claim to start against Manchester City on Sunday.

Šeško has had to wait his turn.

Injured in early May, he sat out all of preseason. A frustrating summer meant he was left on the bench for the first three Premier League games against Hull City, Ipswich Town and Everton.

A goal at Hill Dickinson Stadium earned him a start against Sabah, and he made the most of the opportunity when he collected Bryan Mbeumo's pass late in the first half, rounded the goalkeeper and scored for the second time in five days.

Šeško got 63 minutes before he was substituted for Joshua Zirkzee. It suggests that either the 23-year-old is still working his way back to full fitness or that Carrick is saving his legs for City. We'll find out Sunday.

"It's not an easy decision," Carrick said. "Of course it's not, but it's definitely one I'd prefer to have -- goals in the team and for the boys to be playing well.

"Sometimes it's going to be a start, sometimes it's going to be finishing the game, and we need that within the group from game to game over the season."

If nothing else, Šeško has given Carrick a decision to make. He will perhaps feel he has done enough to play against City, but the question is: Who does he replace?

Mbeumo scored a wonderful solo goal against Everton. Matheus Cunha got his first of the season against Sabah. Marcus Rashford, an unused substitute Thursday, was United's best player last weekend. If Šeško starts in the derby, one would have to drop out.

Perhaps in his favor is that he offers something different to Rashford, Cunha and Mbeumo. He gives United a focal point at No. 9 and a target in the box when the ball goes wide.

He also works hard. Shortly after halftime, he chased down a Sabah defender and wrestled the ball away, prompting a cheer from the Old Trafford crowd nearly as loud as the one when he scored.

"He definitely offers a different kind of threat," Carrick said. "I think that's kind of the beauty of it. That we know what Ben gives us, and there's not many around that give you what Ben does in terms of his physique, his physicality, playing on the last line, his speed to run in behind. He's a real threat.

"It's great to have him back at this level after working to get back to fitness. So, a couple of goals and good performances, good minutes for him. We're really pleased with the way he's gone."

Carrick can also be pleased with United's return to the Champions League. Playing in the competition for the first time since 2023, they dismantled Sabah, a club founded only nine years ago. Tougher tests lie ahead, but four goals and a clean sheet demonstrate a dream start.

"It was what we set out to achieve, really," Carrick said. "I think it was a good performance, individually, collectively, pretty much all the way through the game, from start to finish."

Šeško's form is a positive problem for United's head coach, but he has other selection issues to consider.

Luke Shaw started every Premier League game last season, but there has been debate over the summer about whether his body can cope with extra fixtures in Europe. The early answer is no.

Shaw came off in the 2-2 draw with Everton on Sunday because of cramps and missed training at Carrington on Wednesday morning. The official explanation was that he was given a "designated rest day." Not included in the squad to face Sabah, he had Thursday off, too. It wouldn't be a big issue if there was a designated backup.

Patrick Dorgu, who filled in against Sabah and got the assist for Cunha's opener, has been used as a winger since Carrick came in. Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot can play on the left but prefer the right. Harry Amass, a natural left back, is only 19. A summer bid for Newcastle United's Lewis Hall came to nothing.

Even in early September, it seems Carrick is already having to carefully pick and choose which games Shaw can play. He will hope the England defender is available again for the derby.

The task Sunday has been made more difficult by an uneven schedule that has given Enzo Maresca's team an extra two days to prepare. Carrick said this week it "wasn't ideal."

Preparations for the first Manchester derby of the season have at least been smoothed by a comfortable Champions League victory. Šeško got his goal and made his case to keep his place.

stories.headline: Kings' Kevin Fiala has further surgery, to miss start of camp
stories.summary: Kings forward Kevin Fiala will miss the start of training camp after undergoing follow-up surgery for the broken leg he sustained during the Milan Cortina Olympics.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Kings forward Kevin Fiala will miss the start of training camp after undergoing follow-up surgery for the broken leg he sustained during the Milan Cortina Olympics.

Fiala missed the second half of the NHL season and the playoffs after he was hurt playing for Switzerland in a preliminary round game on Feb. 13. He broke his left femur in a collision with Canada forward Tom Wilson and had to be stretchered off the ice. He had surgery in Italy.

Fiala had 18 goals and 22 assists in 56 games for the Kings last season. The 30-year-old winger has been one of Los Angeles' top offensive contributors since being acquired in a trade from the Minnesota Wild in June 2022 as a restricted free agent. The Kings then signed him to a seven-year contract.

The Kings did not announce a timeline for Fiala's recovery. Los Angeles plays its season opener at the Colorado Avalanche on Sept. 30, a rematch of the four-game sweep that marked the Kings' fifth straight first-round exit.

stories.headline: Team USA scores 108 in rout of Hungary to reach FIBA semis
stories.summary: The U.S. routed Hungary 108-56 to advance to the semifinals of the women's FIBA World Cup and stretched its winning streak in the tournament to 34 games.
stories.body:
BERLIN -- After a scare in the group phase against Italy, Team USA knew it wouldn't be able to play poorly in the knockout rounds of the FIBA World Cup if it wanted to come away with a fifth straight gold medal and 12th overall.

It was only the quarterfinals, but the U.S. responded to that challenge, putting together what the team viewed as its best performance of the tournament with a 108-56 drilling of Hungary. The Americans' 108 points and 31 assists were both records for a World Cup quarterfinal game.

Napheesa Collier led all scorers with 19 points -- a personal best with the senior national team -- followed by 15 from Rhyne Howard and 10 each from Kahleah Copper, Caitlin Clark and Jackie Young.

"We talked about just getting better with each game, and I think we did that today, especially with how we shared [the ball]," Howard said. "I think if we continue to play like that and continue to keep everybody on the same page, continue to move the ball, it's going to be really hard to stop us."

Added Collier: "We were moving the ball a lot. It wasn't one-on-one. We were looking for a great shot, not just a good shot, and so when we play that way, it's really fun. And I feel like our chemistry is building each game."

The U.S. will face either Spain or Australia in Saturday's semifinal, which will tip at 2 p.m. ET.

The Americans got out to a hot start, jumping ahead 36-12 at the end of the first quarter and leading 59-30 at the half. Their defense frustrated Hungary, which saw star post duo Dorka Juhasz and Virag Takacs-Kiss combine for just four points.

The U.S. had 25 of its 44 points off turnovers at the half, using defense to fuel offense on the other end.

"Everybody's just all dialed in offensively and defensively," said Angel Reese, who finished with nine points, six rebounds and three assists. "We talked about our keys, what it's going to take to win gold, and I think tonight we did everything that coach asked us to do."

Two games after Italy held the U.S. to 55 points, the Americans got mostly whatever they wanted offensively. Their 58.8% field goal percentage was their best clip of the tournament, and 12 3-pointers matched their tournament high after shooting 29% from deep in the group stage.

Team USA also won the inside battle Thursday, its 32 paint points at the half (52 overall) were more than the entire Hungary team had scored at that point.

"I feel like today was a really good one for us," Collier said. "We worked on some defensive schemes that we wanted to get better at, some offensive stuff that we wanted to clean up, and so I feel like we went out and executed that."

The 108 points marked the second most scored in a knockout game in World Cup history, behind only Brazil's 110 against the U.S. in the 1994 semifinals. The 52-point win margin was the second largest for a quarterfinal in World Cup history.

"I thought it started with our activity on the defensive end," coach Kara Lawson said. "And so our ability to turn them over, get out in transition, get some advantage plays, 2-on-1, 3-on-2, I thought gave us a lot of confidence early. And then our ability to shoot the 3-point shot ... we have a really good 3-point shooting team, and so I just thought that's what kind of jump-started us."

Lawson and the players agreed the performance was a product of their expedited chemistry-building finally starting to come into fruition. Unlike many national teams, the U.S. did not have a training camp or much prep time together before arriving in Berlin, last gathering as a group (and not its final roster) at the Final Four in April. They have now been together for about 10 days after leaving their WNBA teams.

"The more we play, the more comfortable we're getting with each other," said Young, the only American to hit double figures in each game this tournament. "And tonight we got the ball popping and we were able to get some easy buckets in transition."

Added Collier: "Today felt good, not just because of the score, but in the way that we were scoring as well."

stories.headline: No Ferrari, but Shark is as reliable as they come
stories.summary: After undergoing 15 surgeries during his NRL career, Cameron McInnes revels in the process of recovery and not feeling the best.
stories.body:
Cameron McInnes has made a career out of not feeling comfortable on a rugby league field.

As Cronulla teammate Addin Fonua-Blake put it recently, for more than a decade "that guy has put his face, and not just his body, on the line every week".

By McInnes' own count he has undergone "14 or 15 surgeries" throughout his 243-game NRL career, covering almost every body part with the exception of his shoulders.

All of which, the departing Sharks lock has somewhat enjoyed.

Not because he likes injuries, but the routine and challenge of recovering from them plays right into his hands.

"Some players have to feel like a Ferrari, whereas that's not me," McInnes quips.

"I'm not a car man, but I guess I'm some beaten down thing that does the job.

"I've just learnt to never feel that good out there."

For this entire year, McInnes' approach has had him treating every NRL game as if it may be his last.

It sounds cliche, but last year's surprise diagnosis of an ACL rupture after playing through the pain and later mowing the lawn has taught McInnes to think that way.

This month though, McInnes does know for sure one game will be his last in the NRL, beginning with Saturday night's clash against North Queensland.

Bound for York in the English Super League, McInnes has one month to win a maiden premiership.

"It's really hard, because most footy players are the same. They're so focused on looking to the next thing," McInnes said.

"And because the next week is such a massive opportunity for the club, not just me, for the club, it's still really hard to reflect on (my career) right now.

"I'm not that emotional or sentimental anyway."

For many, the tough-as-nails McInnes is a throwback to another age of rugby league, where beaten up cars were valued in the same way as Ferraris.

But the South Sydney junior is quick to point out that the faster game in fact helped his career, facilitating a move from hooker to a mobile ball-playing lock.

It was in that role he won a NSW State of Origin jersey in 2024, after narrowly missing out as a dummy-half at St George Illawarra in 2018.

McInnes is adamant players like him will always be needed, if not universally recognised.

"The way that the game's covered now, which is great entertainment, it's all about line breaks, tries, those flashy moments," McInnes said.

"Whereas that's probably not been the basis of my game.

"If you ask any coach in the NRL they still value that, but it's just more what the media have to highlight.

"You look at guys that are being talked about and sometimes it's like, oh yeah, it's probably because of those moments they have in games.

"But games go for 80 minutes, not 30 seconds."

stories.headline: Fenerbahce president rejects coach Kartal's resignation after UCL draw
stories.summary: Fenerbahce coach Ismail Kartal announced his shock resignation after the 1-1 draw against Roma, but club president Aziz Yildirim said the coach remains in his position.
stories.body:
Fenerbahce coach İsmail Kartal stunned a post-match news conference following a 1-1 Champions League draw against Roma by announcing his resignation, a move that club president Aziz Yıldırım swiftly rejected.

"I have stepped down tonight," Kartal said. "I made this decision to clear the way for my club. I am resigning with the intention of never returning."

Kartal, who returned to the Istanbul side in June 2026 for his fourth stint, thanked the club for its support and congratulated his players on a match "we could have won," before adding that "from now on, to help Fenerbahçe, my footballers, I have resigned from my position, on the condition of never returning."

The announcement caught club officials entirely off guard, prompting Yıldırım to address the media minutes later to override the manager's decision.

"İsmail Kartal remains in charge. The club must support our coach. As long as I remain president, Kartal is the Fenerbahçe coach," Yıldırım said.

"There is no need for İsmail Kartal to say he will continue. I am his superior; I tell him, 'You will continue,' and that's that."

Playing in front of a sold-out Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium, Fenerbahçe marked their return to Europe's top-tier competition for the first time since the 2008-09 campaign.

Roma opened the scoring when Bryan Cristante capitalized with a low shot from outside the box in the 39th minute. Fenerbahçe responded early in the second half when left back Archie Brown expertly flicked the ball over the goalkeeper to equalize in the 48th minute.

Fenerbahçe will return to action on Monday to face Gaziantep FK in the Turkish Super Lig.
